key_idea: For each digit the number of signs needed is the largest count of that digit in any number up to n, which is achieved by a repdigit: L copies if ddd..d (L digits) <= n, else L-1.
sketch: Let L be the digit count of n. For digit d in 1..9 the answer is L if the L-digit repdigit of d is <= n, otherwise L-1 (the (L-1)-digit repdigit always fits). For digit 0 it is max(1, L-1): the number 0 itself needs one sign and 10^(L-1) has L-1 zeros. Sum the ten values. O(1). Pitfall: digit 0 handled separately (no leading zeros, but 0 itself is displayed), and for single-digit n digits above n need zero signs.
